topics.topic: Whether A21 was reopened or the security review repeated after the A04 amendment
questions: Has the security review been performed again against the amended A04, or is A21 now reopened and incomplete?
Is A21 currently reopened by the A04 change, or is its previous PERFORMED result intended to remain valid for the changed decision without another review?
After the stated change to A04, has the concurrency security review been performed again and accepted, or is A21 reopened and not yet closed?

quotes: A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
judgement.why: Because A04 changed and the concurrency category names A04, A21 is reopened; the unchanged PERFORMED label records the earlier performance but does not override the reopening rule.

topics.topic: Whether A05's repeated-transition invariant applies only after A04 revision validation
questions: Does A05's formal invariant apply only after all A04 checks pass, so a same-state transition carrying a stale revision is refused?

Is A05's formal invariant conditional on passing A04's revision check, so that a repeated transition carrying the old revision is refused, or is every transition to the current state accepted regardless of that stale revision?

quotes:
A transition to the state a record is already in, that passes every check
   of A04 rule 6, is accepted and changes nothing: archiving an archived project (R0-12), anonymising an anonymised
   one (R0-71), erasing an erased Customer (Primary actions), restricting a
   restricted Customer, lifting an unrestricted one, ending an ended
   relationship, resuming one that is not ended (R0-84), granting a project
   already in a session's set, making the active project active again,
   clearing an active project that is already clear, registering a registered
   session (R0-53).
judgement.why: A05 expressly conditions its repeated-transition rule on passing every A04 check, so a supplied former revision fails the revision check first.

topics.topic: How to confirm repeated anonymisation when no revision remains to display or bind
questions: How can Registry show and validate the required confirmation step for anonymising an already anonymised project when there is no revision to show or bind?

quotes:
An action that asks for confirmation (Identity formats) is submitted with a
   confirmation value Registry made when it showed the step: one-time, kept in
   the owner session, bound to the action, its target, the revision or access
   version the step showed, and its inputs — for the import, the file's digest
   and the picks — kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order, never
   as the values themselves; a submission's inputs are bound when their digest
   equals it.

An anonymised project and an
   erased Customer have no revision (M01, M04): an action on them states
   none.

A transition to the state a record is already in, that passes every check
   of A04 rule 6, is accepted and changes nothing: archiving an archived project (R0-12), anonymising an anonymised
   one (R0-71), erasing an erased Customer (Primary actions), restricting a
   restricted Customer, lifting an unrestricted one, ending an ended
   relationship, resuming one that is not ended (R0-84), granting a project
   already in a session's set, making the active project active again,
   clearing an active project that is already clear, registering a registered
   session (R0-53).
judgement.divergence: One implementation binds the confirmation to the explicit absence of a revision and accepts the repeated anonymisation unchanged; another treats A13 as requiring a displayed revision and therefore cannot offer or validate the confirmation, which the owner notices.
judgement.why: The texts require confirmation binding to the revision the step showed and also require this action to state no revision, without saying whether revision absence is itself a bindable confirmation value.

witness.initial: An archived project has been anonymised and therefore has no revision.
events: The owner asks Registry to show the confirmation step for anonymising that project again.
The owner submits the confirmation produced by that step.
outcomes: Registry binds the confirmation to revision absence, accepts the submission and returns the anonymised project unchanged.
Registry cannot bind the confirmation because no revision can be shown, so the step or submission is refused.

topics.topic: Whether the owner interface must send a revision for anonymised or erased records
questions: For an action on an anonymised Project or erased Customer, must the owner interface send no revision as rule 3 requires, or must it somehow send a revision as the Consequence requires?

quotes:
An anonymised project and an
   erased Customer have no revision (M01, M04): an action on them states
   none.

One rule for every record change; the owner interface always shows and sends
the revision of the card it rendered.
judgement.why: One passage requires actions on these records to state no revision, while the other says the interface always sends a revision.

topics.topic: Which refusal takes precedence when deleting an anonymised project with a stale revision
questions: When deletion is submitted with the revision held before the project was anonymised, is it refused as stale or as deletion of an anonymised project?

quotes:
A revision stated for one is not its current one, and the action is
   refused as stale (rule 2): stage (5) of rule 6 applies to it, and comes
   before stage (6) and the refusals of A05 rule 4 — a resubmitted erasure that
   states the revision the record was erased from included; read again, the
   record shows no revision, and the action stating none is answered as
   State 0 and A05 say.
judgement.why: The amended A04 expressly places the stale-revision check before the lifecycle refusal in A05 rule 4, so the result is a stale refusal.
